justification: Assessment returned INVALID, localized the failure to step 0012 (the induction step tacitly freezing dist[v] during an iteration), and gave a different-but-valid witness for the same defect: with s->a(10), s->c(1), c->a(1) and order (s,c),(c,a),(s,a), one in-place pass gives dist[c]=1 then dist[a]=2 while OPT_1(a)=10 (the only <=1-edge s-a path is s->a of length 10); the final relaxation (s,a) yields 10, not < 2, leaving dist[a]=2 < OPT_1(a)=10. That is exactly the ground-truth flaw: the equality form of the loop invariant fails in the direction dist[u] < OPT_k(u) because in-place relaxation propagates along multiple edges within one iteration. It also correctly notes the correct invariant is the inequality.
